text:
jin: Quick flag 1: the Petra-Lite entry in the model_support CSV and the card snippets are using two different field names for the quantized profile. CSV has `quant_profile` but examples and SDK snippets expect `quantization_profile`. SDK integration tests are failing.

sara: yikes. which PR is this?

jin: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/987 (added Petra-Lite). Failing assertion from tests: 
```
AssertionError: missing field 'quantization_profile' in model_card.examples.snippet
Expected keys: name, family, quantization_profile, seq_limit
Found: name, family, quant_profile, seq_limit
```

dan: ok this is a straightforward rename but we should be intentional: add a short migration note and keep a one-release fallback for SDK consumers.

natalie: I'll take the docs side. Plan: (1) update CSV to `quantization_profile`, (2) update model card examples/snippets, (3) add a compatibility blurb in the catalog docs, (4) add a transitional unit test asserting both names are accepted. Taking items 1+2 now.

jin: can you also add an example snippet showing both the legacy and new key so SDK teams can mirror the acceptance behavior?

alex: on the SDK side I already implemented a tolerant parser in sdk-python that falls back to `quant_profile` and emits a deprecation log. I'll open a tiny tests PR to assert both keys pass for the next minor.

sara: while editing the Petra-Lite card, we should correct the seq_limit guidance. Bench claims 8k but quantized runs on small GPUs are closer to 4k due to reduced KV cache. People using Petra-Lite for long-context demos are seeing truncation.

jin: yes. Update Limits section: clarify that quantized variants reduce KV cache; recommend 4096 seq for quantized on small GPUs and link to Optimize guide for quantization tradeoffs.

natalie: proposed note text: 
> Note: Petra-Lite quantized variants have reduced KV cache. For small GPUs, we recommend limiting sequences to 4096 when running quantized. For long contexts prefer non-quantized variants or an extended-kv variant.

dan: add a link to the Optimize/quantization guide and a short CI benchmark command so teams can reproduce perf.

natalie: adding benchmark snippet: 
```
# quick bench example
python bench.py --model petra-lite-quant --seq 4096 --batch 1
```

alex: SDK tests PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/222 1 - includes fallback handling and deprecation warning. CI green on SDK.

jin: can we also include a tiny deprecation blurb in the model catalog changelog so customers scanning release notes see it?

sara: yes. I'll add: "Deprecated field `quant_profile` will be accepted for one release; please migrate to `quantization_profile`. See Petra-Lite migration notes."

docs-bot: reminder: increment the model card frontmatter version and add an entry to models/CHANGELOG.md or lint will fail.

natalie: pushed docs PR that updates CSV, model card limits, migration note, example snippet showing both fields, and canonical Optimize link: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/990

alex: small nit: link checker initially failed because we used a redirecting URL. Natalie fixed to canonical path and force-pushed.

jin: running local integration tests...

alex: SDK CI is green; docs linter green after the link fix. One flaky bench in eu-west region remains but unrelated.

dan: next steps: merge SDK PR (alex), merge docs PR (natalie), and add a short item to the weekly release highlights so Growth can flag Petra-Lite notice. Please copy me on the release note so I can update the benchmark page.

sara: thanks all :tada:
